chunks: It was said to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him): What is the preparation for death? He said: Performing the obligations, avoiding the forbidden, and encompassing oneself with noble virtues — then one does not care whether he approaches death or death approaches him. By Allah, Ibn Abi Talib does not care whether he approaches death or death approaches him.

key_terms.ابن أبي طالب: Ibn Abi Talib — Imam Ali's patronymic, used in first person for emphasis
key_terms.الاستعداد: preparation/readiness — being prepared for death through righteous conduct
key_terms.الفرائض: religious obligations — the mandatory duties prescribed by Islamic law
key_terms.المحارم: the forbidden acts — actions prohibited by divine law (haram)
key_terms.المكارم: noble virtues/generous traits — excellent moral qualities and noble character

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali say one should prepare for death?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam Ali (AS) is asked how to prepare for death. He provides a threefold answer: fulfilling religious obligations (fara'id), avoiding forbidden acts (maharim), and adorning oneself with noble character (makarim). Having done these, one becomes indifferent to death — whether one goes toward it or it comes to him. Imam Ali then personalizes the teaching by swearing that he himself, Ibn Abi Talib, is equally unconcerned about which direction death comes from, demonstrating the sincerity and lived reality of his counsel.
